protocol.purpose: Stress the lexical baseline where the original 15-question set cannot: paraphrases that share few words with the answering chunk, and on-topic questions the corpus does not answer.
protocol.labels: expected_citations lists every chunk a careful reader would accept as directly supporting the answer. Chunks overlap by 40 words, so some answers legitimately appear in two adjacent chunks.

label_status_values.ai_drafted_unverified: Question and label drafted with AI assistance; not yet checked by a person.
label_status_values.human_verified: A person read the cited chunk(s) and confirmed the label unchanged.
label_status_values.human_corrected: A person changed the label; record what changed in label_note.

design_values.paraphrase: Answerable; deliberately avoids the key words of the answering chunk.
design_values.lexical_trap: Answerable; a salient query word also appears in unrelated chunks.
design_values.in_domain_unanswerable: On-topic for the corpus, but no document answers it.

protocol.retriever_settings: Fixed before evaluation and not tuned on this set: TF-IDF exactly as shipped (unigram+bigram, English stop words); BM25 with k1=1.5, b=0.75 using the same token pattern and stop-word list.
protocol.primary_metrics: Chunk-level hit@1, hit@3 and MRR@3 on answerable questions; false-answer and false-abstention rates on the answer/abstain decision.
protocol.threshold_rule: Using the dev split only, choose the abstention threshold from {0} and the observed dev top-1 scores that maximises balanced accuracy of the answer/abstain decision (mean of answer rate on answerable and abstain rate on unanswerable questions); break ties toward the lower threshold. Apply that threshold once to the test split. A question is answered when its top-1 score is positive and at least the threshold.

questions.question: Who does this guidance apply to?
questions.rationale: Chunk 0: the PPN applies to central government departments, their executive agencies and non-departmental public bodies.

questions.question: Are bidders banned from using generative tools when writing proposals?
questions.rationale: Chunk 2: suppliers' use of AI is not prohibited during the commercial process.

questions.question: Why might buyers need to plan for more questions and submissions?
questions.rationale: Chunk 4: suppliers may use AI to streamline bid writing, increasing clarification questions and tender responses.

questions.question: If a purchase raises defence or intelligence worries about supplier AI, who needs to be involved?
questions.rationale: Chunk 5: for national security concerns, engage Information Assurance and Security colleagues before launching. Trap: 'intelligence' also matches 'Artificial Intelligence' throughout Annex A.

questions.question: Why can't text from a chatbot be trusted to be factually correct?
questions.rationale: Chunk 8: LLMs predict statistically plausible text, and plausibility does not mean factual accuracy.

questions.question: Who can I phone with questions about this note?
questions.rationale: Chunk 9: enquiries go to the Crown Commercial Service Helpdesk on 0345 410 2222.

questions.question: Do suppliers' answers about AI use count toward their evaluation score?
questions.rationale: Chunk 14 states the annex questions should not be scored; chunks 15 and 16 label each example question 'For Information Only (Not Scored)'.

questions.question: What must a project write down about how long it holds onto its data?
questions.rationale: Chunk 0: every AI project should record how long its data will be retained.

questions.question: Does a good accuracy number mean the model is ready to deploy?
questions.rationale: Chunk 0: a high score does not establish that a model should be used.

questions.question: What is the maximum fine for a data breach under this policy?
questions.rationale: No document sets fines or penalties.

questions.question: How often must models be retrained?
questions.rationale: No document specifies a retraining cadence.

questions.question: How long must video conference transcripts be retained?
questions.rationale: Chunk 6 discusses meeting transcripts and their use, but no retention period appears anywhere.

questions.question: Which AI vendors are on the government's approved supplier list?
questions.rationale: The PPN names no approved vendors or supplier list.

questions.question: What is the minimum contract value above which AI disclosure becomes mandatory?
questions.rationale: No value threshold appears; disclosure questions are described as optional examples.

questions.question: What is the boiling point of water at sea level?
questions.rationale: Unrelated to the corpus.

questions.question: From what date do the updated rules take effect?
questions.rationale: Chunk 2 (Timing): note the provisions from 24 February 2025. Chunk 1: the updated legislation applies to procurements commenced on or after 24 February 2025.

questions.question: Can a vendor feed our non-public tender papers into a model to train it?
questions.rationale: Chunk 3: controls should stop suppliers using confidential or non-public authority information as AI training data.

questions.question: What checks can a buyer use to confirm a supplier can actually deliver if the bid was AI-written?
questions.rationale: Chunks 3-4: proportionate additional due diligence on capacity and capability, e.g. site visits, clarification questions or supplier presentations.

questions.question: What should buyers do when a service that isn't marketed as AI will still rely on machine learning?
questions.rationale: Chunk 5: AI is increasingly used in 'non-AI' services; commercial teams may require suppliers to declare it and give details.

questions.question: If a meeting tool automatically writes up minutes using AI, what should the contract say about that data?
questions.rationale: Chunks 6-7: contractual terms should make clear that videoconference data is appropriately managed and not used for training unless agreed in writing.

questions.question: Should officials let an AI system make the final call on decisions?
questions.rationale: Chunk 8: decisions should be made with the support of AI systems, not a reliance upon them.

questions.question: What four values does the Turing Institute guidance name?
questions.rationale: Chunk 13 lists the FAST Track Principles: Fairness, Accountability, Sustainability and Transparency. Trap: chunk 12 also names the Turing Institute but not the four values.

questions.question: Can buyers treat vendors differently based on how they answer the AI questions?
questions.rationale: Chunk 15: contracting authorities must not discriminate against suppliers in using these questions or interpreting responses.

questions.question: How is content-creating AI different from earlier kinds of AI?
questions.rationale: Chunk 7: unlike previous forms of AI, generative AI produces new content. Chunks 10-11 repeat the contrast with traditional task-specific models.

questions.question: What should happen once an incident is resolved?
questions.rationale: After recovery, document the root cause, corrective action and prevention work (end of chunk 0, all of chunk 1).

questions.question: What should be written down about overruling a model's output?
questions.rationale: Human oversight: document how a person can override or appeal an output (end of chunk 0, start of chunk 1).

questions.question: Which named official must sign off on using AI in a tender?
questions.rationale: No document names an approving official for AI use in tenders.

questions.question: What is the deadline for reporting an AI incident to the regulator?
questions.rationale: The incident guide covers internal stakeholders; no regulator or deadline appears.

questions.question: What encryption standard must suppliers use for training data?
questions.rationale: No encryption requirement appears anywhere.

questions.question: What budget is allocated for AI training courses for civil servants?
questions.rationale: Chunk 13 lists training resources but no budget.

questions.question: Which large language model does the Cabinet Office recommend for drafting bids?
questions.rationale: No model is recommended; the PPN only discusses risks of LLM use.

questions.question: Who won the 2018 football World Cup?
questions.rationale: Unrelated to the corpus.
